script: I watched the Odyssey remake… they ruined the hero, exposed the gods.. Are you serious??? Nolan literally flipped the whole Odyssey script, like, he rewrote Odysseus into a whole new person, dropped classic characters, tossed in ones that never existed in the poem, invented gods, twisted the Cyclops scene, and rewrote the final test. And then you're freaking out about the skin color of a single woman because "historical accuracy" or whatever? I am like, wow, that's the audacity. I've watched the original epic, the one that taught me about loyalty, cunning, and the long haul home. I know every line of that poem. Then I sat down to see the movie, expecting a faithful adaptation, but it felt like a remix that forgot the original beat. Nolan's version made the hero more narcissistic, the villains less fleshed out, and the gods… well, they were just background props. He even dropped the whole suitor subplot that made the ending so damn satisfying. And here we are, debating a single character's complexion while the real drama is that the film butchered the core story. Like, if you're going to rewrite a classic, at least keep the essence intact. The stakes were clear: my respect for the epic, my love for storytelling, and honestly, my sanity. I couldn't just let this go. The original had depth; the movie had shallow CGI. I felt like I was watching a parody of the real thing. So yeah, you people are such fucking idiots for caring about a detail when the whole narrative was twisted. I am better than that, and honestly, this is the tea. (I know, right?)
